pr_title: feat: don't store to LS during collab
pr_body:
fixes https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/2905

It's a mess — can't guarantee it will work in all cases.

I've refactored collab init a bit in the process to make it a bit more manageable. More to come.

Review [without whitespaces](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/2909/files?diff=split&w=1).

### the problem

In order to skip updating localStorage for collab scenes, we need to know what *is* a collab scene or is tangentially related to it. This sounded simple, but turns out not so.

There are edge cases around starting and existing a collab session where scene gets or may get updated e.g. during scene resetting or otherwise cleaning it up before creating/joining the scene. There are updates trigerred on beforeunload/unload events. They may be late-event updates etc.

### the solution

I've tried to put as much of collab-related updates within a window where the `isCollaborating` flag is set to `true`, and when it is, we skip the LS update.

To make the flag be readable synchronously, I moved it from `CollabWrapper` state to the class instance, to further reduce probability of race conditions.

I'm skipping scene updates when unloading (leaving the page) for the same reason.

---

All in all, I'm not satisfied. The likelihood of failure is still high, and as such this PR leaves a relative safety of a deterministic behavior (always ask at the start) for less safety of an unpredictable one (ask only when stopping the session manually, hoping some lone event won't overwrite the state).

issue_context.title: Losing work due to opening a rooms link
issue_context.body:
I've had a few people reach out to me because they opened a rooms link and that overrode their localStorage content and they lost valuable work as a result.

Another unrelated use case is when integrating the rooms feature into services, the dialog pops up saying that it's going to override local storage content which is not wanted.

Given those two things, I feel like the solution is when we're in a room environment, we disable reading from and writing to localStorage. This way you can open as many rooms links as you want without fearing of losing your work, we don't have the annoying popup. When you reopen the blank excalidraw you get back the work you were working on.

Thoughts?
comments: How should it work when you stop the session instead of close the tab? Should we show the message *then*?
Yeah, that's not a bad idea to put the message then. This is likely a very minor use case so I'm not too concerned about this.

> Another unrelated use case is when integrating the rooms feature into services, the dialog pops up saying that it's going to override local storage content which is not wanted.

Also, you're talking about `<iframe>` integration, right (https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/2902)? We don't officially support that, and there may be other problems with that approach.

review_comments: I don't see it before, did you fix something?
This fixes a case where you load a room and then leave it immediately, so that it doesn't bother you with "unsaved data prompt"
Btw, in-code comments are really useful for those. Whenever some line of code is not obvious what it's doing it's a good idea to add a comment.
How hard would it be to make it a function instead? I really don't like getters as they give the wrong mental model to people reading the code.
Can you promise.all the two calls so that they don't need to wait on each other?

Thought about it while I was refactoring this method, but it seemed like a micro-optim.

Just tested. It takes 0.4ms, and parallelizing it actually tends to increase it by 0.1ms at times, and makes it less readable :).
